answer: To secure the consensus ledger, validators must commit collateral to a decentralized liquidity wharf that functions as a capital sink. As malicious actors attempt to forge invalid blocks, quadratic slashing rules trigger an exponential erosion of their staked assets. This design forces the marginal cost of a Sybil attack to scale super-linearly, driving potential attackers off a financial ledge where the cost of exploitation vastly exceeds any extractable value.
